messages:
Andrew: high-sev from ACME — their Private deployment in eu-central-1 has started hitting intermittent Decrypt 403s since last-night key migration to a KMS custom key store (CloudHSM). customer impact: writes failing, app retries, billing spike. sending logs below. 

Priya: can you paste the exact KMS error blob and a repro CLI command? also which alias/key-id was migrated? @Maya fyi.

Andrew: key-id = arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345, alias = alias/acme-prod, migration window 03:00-04:00 UTC. CLI repro: 
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --encryption-context Key=tenant_id,Value=acme-123 --region eu-central-1 --profile acme-prod
```
Error: 
```
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:... (status code: 403)
Debug: RequestId: 8f7b2c...
```

Lee: curious — is this cross-account or same acct? any grants?

Andrew: same account. We use a custom key store (CKS) backed by CloudHSM cluster. No cross-account grants. Key policy is fairly locked down (only KMS service role + customer principal via kms:ViaService condition for our private control plane).

Maya: two quick angles: (1) alias swap/cache on our side after migration (aliases may still point to old key id in some caches) (2) encryption-context enforcement: KMS will deny if the provided context doesn't match exactly. show me the ciphertext metadata.

Andrew: ciphertext metadata from our vault logs: 
`encryption_context={"tenant_id":"acme-123","request_id":"req-9987"}`
But interestingly, the failing decrypt attempts on customer side show empty encryption context in our logging (they're sending no tenant_id). snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T03:15:22Z ERROR decrypt failed id=req-9987 status=403 ctx="{}" user=svc-acme
```

Priya: hmm. that implies something mutated the request between client and KMS. Could our KMS proxy (kms-proxy in Private deployments) be dropping or normalizing the EncryptionContext header when it times out/retries?

Andrew: ops-bot recorded a 504 to the proxy around 03:12:xx and client retried. Full proxy log: 
```
[03:12:07] proxied-decrypt request id=req-9987 start
[03:12:07] upstream KMS TLS handshake delayed 1.6s
[03:12:08] proxied-decrypt forwarded retry without ctx header due to bug #1342
[03:12:08] proxied-decrypt upstream 403 from KMS
```

Lee: whoa — "forwarded retry without ctx header" — that's a smoking gun. That bug number sounds like a middleware header drop on 5xx/timeout retry paths. I thought we fixed 1342 in the hosted proxy earlier this year but maybe not for private CKS path.

Maya: agreed. if retry removes EncryptionContext then KMS will 403. We should treat this as a security escalation because it caused data access failures and a customer outage. @oncall (Priya) please open an incident and loop CloudHSM/KMS infra.

Priya: opening incident now: INC-2026-0315-1745. Initial triage: rollback proxy retry change for private deployments, add a guard to preserve EncryptionContext on retries, and add regression test.

Andrew: customer wants a mitigation ASAP. Can we temporarily route their decrypts to hosted KMS path (non-CKS) or add an allowlist to bypass retries?

Lee: short-term options: (A) fail fast on 504 so client retries end-to-end (won't strip headers) (B) flip their private deployment to use the hosted KMS path (requires alias remap and a short outage) (C) add a proxy patch to preserve headers on retry — likely fastest if we can ship a config toggle and hot-restart the proxy.

Maya: security note — option B (hosted KMS) means we need customer approval for key material not in their CloudHSM; also audit entry required. Get signed waiver.

Priya: executing plan B + C in parallel: contacting customer for consent to remap alias to hosted path for 10m, and ops will prepare a proxy patch to preserve EncryptionContext on retry. rollback plan ready.

Support-Bot: Noted. Customer ticket #CS-5882 updated with incident link and status = remediation in progress.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline queued for: kms-proxy v2.4.3-hotfix (preserve-ctx-on-retry) — ETA 12m to canary in eu-central-1.

Andrew: thanks — keep notes of exact timestamps and audit IDs; we'll need them for postmortem and for the customer's compliance team. Also audit log shows a small billing delta from extra decrypt attempts ~+1200 ops during the window.

Maya: tagging for postmortem: require timeline, root cause (proxy header-drop bug), impact (customer requests failed, billing delta), and corrective actions (fix + tests + instrumentation), plus a new alert on proxy header-drop rate.

Lee: I'll push the hotfix to canary and monitor decrypt success rates. ping me if the hosted remap is approved so we can cutover.

Andrew: customer approved hosted remap at 03:28 UTC. switchover done, their decrypts started succeeding immediately. we'll keep canary running and follow-up with patch release and postmortem. :thumbsup:
